messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis

Details:
The failing test `testSingleOptionSingleArgument` illustrates that when parsing command-line arguments with default values specified for multiple expected arguments, the behavior is counter-intuitive. The test sets up a parser with default values `["100", "1000"]` for an option `-b`, but when passing a single argument `1` for `-b`, the return values are `["1", "1000"]` instead of just `["1"]`.

Inspection of the `Parser.parse(String[])` method reveals that it sets up a WriteableCommandLine and calls `group.defaults(commandLine)` to initialize defaults before processing the arguments. It then iteratively processes the input arguments.

The key method involved in returning values is `CommandLineImpl.getValues(String)` which delegates to the overloaded `getValues(Option, List)` with an empty list as the default values. The `WriteableCommandLineImpl.getValues(Option, List)` method shows how defaults are combined:

- It first tries to get the stored values associated with the option.
- If no values or empty list, it initializes the list from the passed-in defaultValues.
- If still empty, it uses the internal defaultValues stored.
- Finally, it returns the value list (or empty if none).

In the failing test scenario, the defaults are preset as `["100", "1000"]`. Passing one argument `1` results in the stored values being `["1"]`. The method then picks the default values from the internal default list and "augments" the stored value list with them. This augmentation logic is problematic—it adds default values even when some values are provided by the user.

Thus, when one argument `1` is passed, the result ends up as `["1", "1000"]` because the logic appends remaining default values instead of replacing or truncating correctly to match actual arguments.

The bug report summary confirms this: default arguments are only picked up when no arguments are submitted at all; passing partial arguments leads to unexpected mixed results.

In short, the root cause is in the default value handling logic in `WriteableCommandLineImpl.getValues` which augments user-provided values with default values if the list is partially empty, leading to counter-intuitive behavior when multiple arguments with defaults exist.

Recent bug reports do not relate directly to default values or argument parsing in this way and thus do not add relevant context.

This diagnosis aligns with the failing test code and explains why the test fails as observed.

Next step: fix the default value handling in `WriteableCommandLineImpl.getValues(Option, List)` to better handle partial argument input scenarios.

Would you like me to suggest which methods should be fixed based on this diagnosis?

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
